approaches.name: Palmar approach to the proximal interphalangeal joint
aliases: volar Bruner approach to the PIP joint
shotgun approach to the PIP joint
approaches.corridor: Volar Bruner interval through the flexor sheath between the A2 and A4 pulleys, retracting the flexor tendons and detaching the volar plate to open the PIP joint

sources.title: Palmar approach to the proximal interphalangeal joint
Volar approach to the metacarpophalangeal joint
Palmar approach to PIP joint (middle-phalanges collection)

procedure_applications.condition: A volar PIP fracture-dislocation or intra-articular base of middle phalanx fracture needs open joint access

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Use the palmar flexor skin creases as a guide, with the incision apex at the intermediate crease over the PIP joint.

incision.text: Make a carefully planned Bruner zig-zag palmar incision using the flexor creases.

superficial_interval.text: Elevate thin skin flaps and identify and gently mobilize the digital arteries and nerves on each side.

deep_interval.text: Incise the C1, A3, and C2 pulleys laterally near their bony attachments leaving a cuff for repair, preserve the A2 and A4 pulleys, retract the flexor tendons with a loop, and detach the volar plate as a flap.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with digital neurovascular bundles, flexor sheath and pulleys, flexor tendons, volar plate, and the PIP joint.

structures_at_risk.text: The digital arteries and nerves on each side, the vincular arteries to the flexor tendons, and the A2 and A4 pulleys are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The lateral borders of the sheath are the danger zones for the digital neurovascular bundles; cutting the A2 or A4 pulleys risks tendon bowstringing.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the mobilized digital neurovascular bundles gently and preserve the vincular blood supply to the flexor tendons.

exposure.text: Opens the volar PIP joint fully, and dividing both collateral ligaments allows hyperextension (shotgun) exposure for comminuted fractures.

limitations.text: Preservation of the A2 and A4 pulleys constrains proximal and distal extension, and wide exposure requires collateral ligament release.

indications.text: Indicated for volar PIP fracture-dislocations and intra-articular fractures of the base of the middle phalanx.

closure.text: Repair the volar plate with pullout or anchor sutures and reattach the A3 and, where possible, the C1 and C2 pulleys with nonabsorbable monofilament.

complications.text: Complications include digital nerve injury, flexor tendon bowstringing from pulley loss, PIP stiffness, and skin flap problems.

questions.question: Which pulleys must be preserved in the palmar PIP approach?
What is the shotgun maneuver for PIP exposure?
questions.answer: Dividing both collateral ligaments to hyperextend and fully open the joint.

questions.question: Which structures must be mobilized and protected in the skin flaps?

approaches.name: Volar approach to the metacarpophalangeal joint
aliases: palmar approach to the MCP joint
approaches.corridor: Volar Z-incision over the MCP joint through the A1 pulley region, retracting the flexor tendons to reach the volar plate and joint, protecting the collateral digital nerves

sources.title: Volar approach to the metacarpophalangeal joint
Palmar approach to the proximal interphalangeal joint
Volar approach to the MCP joints (metacarpals)

procedure_applications.condition: An irreducible volar MCP dislocation or metacarpal head fracture needs open volar access

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the MCP joint level and the palmar skin creases.

incision.text: Make a Z-shaped incision over the MCP joint with the apex radial or ulnar at a skin crease, extending proximally in Z-fashion along the creases to avoid contracture.

superficial_interval.text: Expose the flexor retinaculum and A1 pulley and identify the collateral neurovascular bundles, remembering the digital nerve may be displaced volarly with the metacarpal head after dislocation.

deep_interval.text: Sharply dissect the flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus off the volar plate and capsule and retract them to expose the volar joint.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with collateral digital nerves, flexor retinaculum and A1 pulley, flexor tendons, volar plate, and the MCP joint.

structures_at_risk.text: The collateral neurovascular bundles of the digit and the common digital nerve are at risk, especially when a nerve is displaced volarly with the metacarpal head.

danger_zones.text: The volar-displaced metacarpal head region is the danger zone because the digital nerve can be draped over it.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid overretraction to prevent nerve damage and keep multiple incisions spaced to prevent skin flap ischemia.

exposure.text: Exposes the volar MCP joint and any interposed ruptured capsule after dislocation.

limitations.text: The volar approach gives limited access to the dorsal joint and depends on careful digital nerve identification.

indications.text: Indicated for irreducible volar MCP dislocation and selected volar MCP joint pathology.

closure.text: Repair the joint capsule with fine sutures, reposition the flexor tendons, and do not repair the A1 pulley to avoid tendon sheath contracture.

complications.text: Complications include digital nerve injury, skin flap ischemia, and MCP stiffness.

questions.question: Why is a Z-shaped incision used over the MCP joint?
questions.answer: To respect the skin creases and avoid contracture.

questions.question: Why is the A1 pulley not repaired at closure?
questions.answer: Because repair may cause tendon sheath contracture and restrict flexor excursion.

questions.question: Where may the digital nerve lie after a volar MCP dislocation?
questions.answer: Displaced volarly, draped over the metacarpal head.

approaches.name: Pediatric anterolateral approach to the humeral shaft
approaches.corridor: Anterolateral interval between biceps/brachialis medially and the mobile wad laterally, splitting brachialis in the plane between the radial and musculocutaneous nerves to reach the anterior humerus

sources.title: Anterolateral approach to the humeral shaft (pediatric)
Extended deltopectoral approach to the humeral shaft

procedure_applications.condition: A pediatric proximal or midshaft humeral fracture is plated through an anterior interval

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a hand table and the shoulder to distal arm accessible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the deltopectoral interval proximally and the biceps and mobile wad interval distally.

incision.text: Follow a line from the interval between biceps and the mobile wad distally to the deltopectoral interval proximally.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the fascia between biceps/brachialis and the mobile wad, retract the biceps medially and the mobile wad laterally, identifying the cephalic vein proximally.

deep_interval.text: Split the brachialis in the plane between the radial and musculocutaneous nerves to keep its dual innervation and protect the radial nerve where it perforates the lateral intermuscular septum.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, the biceps/brachialis and mobile wad interval, the split brachialis, and the anterior humerus.

structures_at_risk.text: The radial nerve perforating the lateral intermuscular septum, the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm distally, and the musculocutaneous nerve are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The distal lateral humerus where the radial nerve perforates the septum is the danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Split brachialis in its midline to protect the radial nerve laterally and keep the mobile wad retraction gentle.

exposure.text: Exposes the anterior surface of the proximal and mid humerus.

limitations.text: Distal extension is limited by the radial nerve, and very distal fractures may need a separate exposure.

indications.text: Indicated for plating of pediatric proximal and midshaft humeral fractures.

closure.text: Close the subcutaneous tissues and skin in layers with absorbable sutures.

complications.text: Complications include radial nerve palsy, lateral forearm cutaneous nerve injury, and wound problems.

questions.question: In what nerve plane is the brachialis split in the anterolateral humeral approach?
questions.answer: Between the radial and musculocutaneous nerves.

questions.question: Where does the radial nerve enter the anterior compartment?
questions.answer: By perforating the lateral intermuscular septum distally.

questions.question: Why split brachialis rather than take it off one side?
questions.answer: To preserve its dual radial and musculocutaneous innervation.
